STEP 1 - Scene: This is not really a meal; it is a single whole orange (mandarin/tangerine-sized, slightly flattened) sitting on a white plate or tray with some faint orange stains. It is photographed from above at an oblique, tilted angle, with a white bowl partly visible at the bottom right.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white vessel is an irregular, roughly fan-shaped dish about 26 cm across its longest undistorted width, so treat it as a dinner plate. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. The orange is about 8 cm in diameter by comparison with the plate's width, which is consistent with a medium orange.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole orange (fresh fruit, peel on).

STEP 4 - Area: The orange covers roughly 5% of the plate area (about 27 cm^2 projected, since the orange is roughly 8 cm across).

STEP 5 - Volume: An orange is roughly spherical; its volume is about 4/3 x 3.14 x (4)^3 ≈ 268 ml. Using the projected area and a ~8 cm height gives a similar envelope, so take ~250 ml as the gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit is dense, roughly 1.0 g/ml when measured as a whole piece (it is not a loose pile). A medium orange typically weighs about 130-170 g; with the visible size I estimate about 150 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Orange flesh and peel-on whole fruit is about 47 kcal per 100 g. 150 g x 0.47 = about 70 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium orange at ~150 g and ~70 kcal is plausible for a single visible piece of fruit. There is no other food on the plate.

Total: about 150 g, about 70 kcal.
